/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
  The report: one row per rule and grounding, with support, episode verdict, timeline, the
  histogram of unknown reasons, residues and the surrogate flag; rendered as tab-separated text
  (the gate's contract) and as JSON lines (the diagnosis tooling's).

  It composes everything below it and owns nothing else. The row format is a contract with
  `tools/check_spec.py` and `scripts/diagnostics/`; changing a line here is a cross-artifact change.
  Surrogate rows never enter the concrete tallies.

  Text format (tab-separated; one record per line):
    SOURCE   source  instants=N  gap=<seconds>
    RULE     rule  concrete|surrogate  support  absent-ids(,)  groundings=N  live=bool  v=N c=N na=N u=N
    GROUND   rule  grounding  episode
    TL       rule  grounding  t_from  t_to  verdict            (runs of equal verdict, ms timestamps)
    UNK      rule  grounding  reason  count
    RESIDUE  rule  text
    SUMMARY  concrete|surrogate  rules=N supported=N partial=N unsupported=N live=N v=N c=N na=N u=N
-/
import Lean.Data.Json
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Monitor
open Grounding

structure Row where
  rule : String
  surrogate : Bool
  support : Support
  grounding : Grounding
  episode : Verdict
  timeline : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  unknowns : List (String × Nat)
  residues : List String
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure RuleLine where
  rule : String
  surrogate : Bool
  support : Support
  groundings : Nat
  live : Bool
  violated : Nat
  compliant : Nat
  notApplicable : Nat
  unknown : Nat
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure Report where
  source : String
  instants : Nat
  gap : Q
  rules : List RuleLine
  rows : List Row
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

def histogram (tl : List Verdict) : List (String × Nat) :=
  let tags := tl.flatMap fun v => (v.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag).eraseDups
  tags.eraseDups.map fun t => (t, tags.count t)

def countVerdict (vs : List Verdict) (p : Verdict → Bool) : Nat := (vs.filter p).length
def isUnknown : Verdict → Bool | .unknown _ => true | _ => false

/-- Evaluate a rule set over one trace as the source would have produced it, the rules' concept
    calls expanded over `cs`. Unsupported rules are reported without groundings: nothing they
    say could be decided. A trace the admission rejects is not evaluated: its defects are returned. -/
def check (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (m : Manifest) (cs : List Concept := []) : Except (List String) Report := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule cs)
  let S ← Setup.admit rules (maskTrace m τ) ρ m.reidGap
  let per := rules.map fun r =>
    let sup := support rules r m
    match sup with
    | .unsupported _ => ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := 0, live := false,
                           violated := 0, compliant := 0, notApplicable := 0, unknown := 0 : RuleLine }, ([] : List Row))
    | _ =>
      let evaluated : List (Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) := Grounding.check S r
      let rows : List Row := evaluated.map fun (e : Grounding × Grounding.Timeline × Verdict) =>
        let g := e.1; let tl := e.2.1; let ep := e.2.2
        let vs : List Verdict := tl.verdicts.toList.map Prod.snd
        { rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, grounding := g, episode := ep,
          timeline := tl.verdicts, unknowns := histogram vs, residues := r.residues }
      let eps : List Verdict := rows.map Row.episode
      ({ rule := r.id, surrogate := r.surrogate, support := sup, groundings := rows.length,
         live := evaluated.any (fun e => e.2.1.live),
         violated := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.violated), compliant := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.compliant),
         notApplicable := countVerdict eps (· == Verdict.notApplicable), unknown := countVerdict eps isUnknown : RuleLine }, rows)
  pure { source := m.source, instants := τ.length, gap := m.reidGap, rules := per.map (·.1), rows := per.flatMap (·.2) }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Text
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def qText (q : Q) : String :=
  let g := Nat.gcd q.num.natAbs q.den
  let g := if g == 0 then 1 else g
  let n := q.num / (Int.ofNat g)
  let d := q.den / g
  if d == 1 then toString n else s!"{n}/{d}"
def tabs (xs : List String) : String := String.intercalate "\t" xs
def kind (surrogate : Bool) : String := if surrogate then "surrogate" else "concrete"

/-- Runs of equal verdicts: (from, to, verdict). -/
def runs (tl : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)) : List (Timestamp × Timestamp × Verdict) :=
  tl.toList.foldl (fun acc (t, v) =>
    match acc with
    | (a, _, v') :: rest => if v' == v then (a, t, v) :: rest else (t, t, v) :: acc
    | [] => [(t, t, v)]) [] |>.reverse

def rowLines (row : Row) : List String :=
  let g := row.grounding.render
  [tabs ["GROUND", row.rule, g, row.episode.tag]] ++
  ((runs row.timeline).map fun (a, b', v) => tabs ["TL", row.rule, g, toString a, toString b', v.tag]) ++
  (row.unknowns.map fun (t, n) => tabs ["UNK", row.rule, g, t, toString n])

def ruleLine (l : RuleLine) : String :=
  tabs ["RULE", l.rule, kind l.surrogate, l.support.tag, String.intercalate "," l.support.absent,
        s!"groundings={l.groundings}", s!"live={l.live}",
        s!"v={l.violated}", s!"c={l.compliant}", s!"na={l.notApplicable}", s!"u={l.unknown}"]

def summaryLine (surrogate : Bool) (ls : List RuleLine) : String :=
  let ls := ls.filter (·.surrogate == surrogate)
  let n (p : RuleLine → Bool) := (ls.filter p).length
  let sum (f : RuleLine → Nat) := ls.foldl (fun a l => a + f l) 0
  tabs ["SUMMARY", kind surrogate, s!"rules={ls.length}",
        s!"supported={n (·.support == .supported)}",
        s!"partial={n fun l => match l.support with | .partially _ => true | _ => false}",
        s!"unsupported={n fun l => match l.support with | .unsupported _ => true | _ => false}",
        s!"live={n (·.live)}", s!"v={sum (·.violated)}", s!"c={sum (·.compliant)}",
        s!"na={sum (·.notApplicable)}", s!"u={sum (·.unknown)}"]

def renderText (rep : Report) : String :=
  let header := tabs ["SOURCE", rep.source, s!"instants={rep.instants}", s!"gap={qText rep.gap}"]
  let ruleBlocks := rep.rules.flatMap fun l =>
    let residues : List String := ((rep.rows.find? (·.rule == l.rule)).map (·.residues)).getD []
    [ruleLine l] ++
    (rep.rows.filter (·.rule == l.rule)).flatMap rowLines ++
    residues.map fun t => tabs ["RESIDUE", l.rule, t]
  String.intercalate "\n" ([header] ++ ruleBlocks ++ [summaryLine false rep.rules, summaryLine true rep.rules]) ++ "\n"

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- JSON lines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
open Lean in
def verdictJson (v : Verdict) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [("verdict", v.tag), ("reasons", Json.arr (v.reasons.map fun r => Json.str r.tag).toArray)]

open Lean in
def rowJson (row : Row) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [
    ("kind", "grounding"), ("rule", row.rule), ("surrogate", row.surrogate), ("support", row.support.tag),
    ("grounding", Json.mkObj (row.grounding.assign.map fun (n, t) => (n, Json.num t))),
    ("episode", verdictJson row.episode),
    ("timeline", Json.arr ((runs row.timeline).map fun (a, b', v) =>
        Json.mkObj [("from", Json.num a), ("to", Json.num b'), ("verdict", v.tag)]).toArray),
    ("unknowns", Json.mkObj (row.unknowns.map fun (t, n) => (t, Json.num n))),
    ("residues", Json.arr (row.residues.map Json.str).toArray)]

open Lean in
def ruleJson (l : RuleLine) : Json :=
  Json.mkObj [
    ("kind", "rule"), ("rule", l.rule), ("surrogate", l.surrogate), ("support", l.support.tag),
    ("absent", Json.arr (l.support.absent.map Json.str).toArray), ("groundings", Json.num l.groundings),
    ("live", l.live), ("violated", Json.num l.violated), ("compliant", Json.num l.compliant),
    ("not_applicable", Json.num l.notApplicable), ("unknown", Json.num l.unknown)]

open Lean in
def renderJsonLines (rep : Report) : String :=
  let header := Json.mkObj [("kind", "source"), ("source", rep.source), ("instants", Json.num rep.instants), ("gap", qText rep.gap)]
  String.intercalate "\n" ((header :: rep.rules.map ruleJson ++ rep.rows.map rowJson).map (·.compress)) ++ "\n"

end Monitor
end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TRAINING SPLIT variant, generated by harness/tools/split.py from the full file: the lines that read the
3	  atoms the split omits are removed. Do not edit; regenerate.
4	-/
5	/-
6	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest
7	  What a source can observe: a capability per atom id, complete over ATOMS.md (`subject` is an atom
8	  observed for the subject track alone, as an instrumented vehicle reports its own controls); a mask
9	  that blanks every field of an absent atom, and of a subject-only atom on every other road user,
10	  before evaluation; and `support`, the first and most honest number
11	  a source gets — which rules it can be judged against at all, computed from the rules' syntax
12	  before any frame is read.
13	
14	  The same rules run on a simulator, on an annotated dataset and on perception over video; the
15	  only thing that differs is what each can see, and that difference is a declared input here.
16	  For the perception stage the manifest is the interface the other way round: the list of atoms
17	  its programs must deliver, with the error class each is allowed.
18	-/
19	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
20	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Semantics
21	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Ontology.Ids
22	
23	namespace TrafficSpec
24	
25	inductive Capability
26	  | exact
27	  | estimate (errorClass : String)
28	  | absent
29	  | subject
30	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
31	
32	structure Manifest where
33	  source : String
34	  entries : List (String × Capability)     -- atom id in ATOMS.md form ↦ capability
35	  /-- The longest tracker break the source's re-identification links may bridge (seconds). -/
36	  reidGap : Q := Q.zero
37	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
38	
39	namespace Manifest
40	/-- An atom the manifest does not list is absent: silence is not a capability. -/
41	def capability (m : Manifest) (id : String) : Capability :=
42	  ((m.entries.find? (·.1 == id)).map (·.2)).getD .absent
43	def observes (m : Manifest) (id : String) : Bool := m.capability id != .absent
44	/-- Complete: every atom id of ATOMS.md has an entry, and no entry names anything else. -/
45	def complete (m : Manifest) : Bool :=
46	  atomIds.all (fun id => (m.entries.find? (·.1 == id)).isSome) &&
47	  m.entries.all (fun e => atomIds.contains e.1)
48	def absentIds (m : Manifest) : List String := atomIds.filter fun id => !m.observes id
49	/-- The atoms observed for the subject track only. -/
50	def subjectIds (m : Manifest) : List String := atomIds.filter fun id => m.capability id == .subject
51	/-- A manifest that observes everything exactly (the simulator's, and the tests'). -/
52	def full (source : String) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
53	  { source := source, entries := atomIds.map fun id => (id, .exact), reidGap := gap }
54	end Manifest
55	
56	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	-- From Lean names back to atom ids
58	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	/-- The atom id a Lean name reads: the longest id whose `defName` is a prefix of the name
60	    (`dev_traffic_signal_shows` ↦ `dev.traffic_signal`), with the relation aliases spelled out. -/
61	def atomIdOf (name : String) : Option String :=
62	  let n := match name with
63	    | "rel_ahead_in_lane" | "rel_behind_in_lane" => "rel_ahead_behind_in_lane"
64	    | other => other
65	  let cands := atomIds.filter fun id =>
66	    let d := Semantics.defName id
67	    n == d || n.startsWith (d ++ "_")
68	  cands.foldl (fun acc id => match acc with
69	    | none => some id
70	    | some a => if id.length > a.length then some id else some a) none
71	
72	/-- The atom ids a read of `id` depends on: itself, and for a read of a region kind or of a relation
73	    that reads kind membership, the kinds whose masks its verdict follows (a kind's ancestors; a
74	    lane relation's lane kind; an entrance's line kinds, stop line and crosswalk). No source
75	    declares an abstract kind: a read of one depends on the kinds refining it directly, and no read
76	    depends on an abstract ancestor. -/
77	def kindDependencies (id : String) : List String :=
78	  let kinds (ks : List StructureKind) := (ks.filter (!·.isAbstract)).map fun k => s!"st.{k}"
79	  let ofKind (k : StructureKind) :=
80	    if k.isAbstract then kinds (StructureKind.all.filter (·.parent? == some k))
81	    else kinds (k :: k.ancestors)
82	  match id with
83	  | "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane" => id :: ofKind .lane
84	  | "st.entrance_of" => id :: ofKind .stopLine ++ ofKind .crosswalk
85	  | _ =>
86	    if id.startsWith "st." then
87	      match StructureKind.ofString ((id.drop 3).toString) with
88	      | some k => ofKind k
89	      | none => [id]
90	    else [id]

92	/-- The atom ids a formula list reads, through atoms and primitives (a concept call is expanded first). -/
93	def formulaAtomIds (fs : List Formula) : List String :=
94	  ((fs.flatMap Formula.atoms).flatMap fun n =>
95	    if n.startsWith "prim_" then (Primitives.reads n).filterMap atomIdOf
96	    else (atomIdOf n).toList).flatMap kindDependencies |>.eraseDups
97	
98	/-- The atom ids a rule reads, through its atoms, its primitives and, transitively, the
99	    rules it composes. -/
100	def Rule.atomIds (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List String :=
101	  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (r : Rule) : List String :=
102	    match fuel with
103	    | 0 => formulaAtomIds r.formulas
104	    | fuel + 1 =>
105	      formulaAtomIds r.formulas ++ (r.composes.flatMap fun id =>
106	        if seen.contains id then [] else
107	        match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
108	        | some r' => go fuel (id :: seen) r'
109	        | none => [])
110	  (go rules.length [r.id] r).eraseDups
111	
112	inductive Support
113	  | supported
114	  | partially (absent : List String)      -- some atoms unobserved: verdicts may be unknown
115	  | unsupported (absent : List String)    -- the obligation reads nothing the source observes
116	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
117	
118	def Support.tag : Support → String
119	  | .supported => "supported"
120	  | .partially _ => "partial"
121	  | .unsupported _ => "unsupported"
122	def Support.absent : Support → List String
123	  | .supported => []
124	  | .partially a | .unsupported a => a

126	/-- Support from syntax alone, closed over the rules a rule composes. Unsupported when every atom
127	    the obligation reads is absent (the rule could never decide), or a binder's class can never be
128	    established, or a composed rule is itself unsupported. -/
129	def support (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (m : Manifest) : Support :=
130	  -- the clock is every source's: a window over time reads it, and no manifest declares it absent
131	  let absentOf (fs : List Formula) : List String × Nat :=
132	    let ids := (formulaAtomIds fs).filter (· != "kin.time")
133	    (ids.filter fun id => !m.observes id, ids.length)
134	  let (oblAbsent, oblTotal) := absentOf [r.obligation]
135	  let clsDead := r.binders.any fun b =>
136	    let (a, n) := absentOf [b.cls]
137	    n > 0 && a.length == n
138	  let composedDead := (r.composes.filterMap fun id => rules.find? (·.id == id)).any fun r' =>
139	    let (a, n) := absentOf [r'.obligation]
140	    n > 0 && a.length == n
141	  let allAbsent := (Rule.atomIds rules r).filter fun id => !m.observes id
142	  if allAbsent.isEmpty then .supported
143	  else if clsDead || composedDead || (oblTotal > 0 && oblAbsent.length == oblTotal) then .unsupported allAbsent
144	  else .partially allAbsent

152	  | "ru.subject" => u
153	  | "ru.occupant_count" => { u with occupants := none }
154	  | "ru.rider_posture" => { u with posture := {} }
155	  | "kin.position" => { u with kin := { u.kin with position := none } }
156	  | "kin.heading" => { u with kin := { u.kin with heading := none } }
157	  | "kin.velocity" => { u with kin := { u.kin with velocity := none } }
158	  | "kin.speed" => { u with kin := { u.kin with speed := none } }
159	  | "kin.accel_longitudinal" => { u with kin := { u.kin with accelLongitudinal := none } }
160	  | "kin.yaw_rate" => { u with kin := { u.kin with yawRate := none } }
161	  | "kin.extent" => { u with kin := { u.kin with extent := none } }
162	  | "kin.steer_angle" => { u with kin := { u.kin with steerAngle := none } }
163	  | "kin.path_length" => { u with kin := { u.kin with pathLength := none } }
164	  | "kin.engine_running" => { u with kin := { u.kin with engineRunning := none } }
165	  | "kin.parking_brake" => { u with kin := { u.kin with parkingBrake := none } }
166	  | "kin.gear" => { u with kin := { u.kin with gear := none } }
167	  | "kin.throttle" => { u with kin := { u.kin with throttle := none } }
168	  | "kin.service_brake" => { u with kin := { u.kin with serviceBrake := none } }
169	  | "sig.turn_indicator" => { u with sig := { u.sig with turnIndicator := none } }
170	  | "sig.brake_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with brakeLamp := none } }
171	  | "sig.hazard" => { u with sig := { u.sig with hazard := none } }
172	  | "sig.headlamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with headlamp := none } }
173	  | "sig.position_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with positionLamp := none } }
174	  | "sig.warning_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with warningLamps := none } }
175	  | "sig.siren" => { u with sig := { u.sig with siren := none } }
176	  | "sig.horn" => { u with sig := { u.sig with horn := none } }
177	  | "sig.hand_signal" => { u with sig := { u.sig with handSignal := none } }
178	  | "ru.aggregate" => { u with classes := none }   -- the source classifies nothing: every member unknown
179	  | "sig.door_open" => { u with sig := { u.sig with doorsOpen := none } }
180	  | "sig.compression_brake" => { u with sig := { u.sig with compressionBrake := none } }
181	  | "st.sight_along_way" => { u with sightAlongWay := none }
182	  | _ =>

196	  match id with
197	  | "st.lane_direction" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with direction := none } }
198	  | "st.lane_adjacency" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l =>
199	      { l with leftNeighbour := none, rightNeighbour := none, ordinalFromLeft := none, countInDirection := none } }
200	  | "st.lane_connectivity" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with leadsTo := none } }
201	  | "st.lane_enters" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with entersIntersection := none } }
202	  | "st.lane_marking" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with markingLeft := none, markingRight := none } }
203	  | "st.lane_width" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with width := none } }

214	    match StructureKind.ofString ((id.drop 3).toString) with
215	    | some k => if k.isAbstract then some st else some { st with unobservedKinds := k :: st.unobservedKinds }

223	  | _ =>

226	    | some k => some { d with unobservedKinds := k :: d.unobservedKinds }
227	    | none => some d

232	  | "env.precipitation" => { e with precipitation := none }
233	  | "env.wet_road" => { e with wetRoad := none }
234	  | "env.ice_or_snow" => { e with iceOrSnow := none }
235	  | "env.visibility" => { e with visibility := none }
236	  | "env.civil_time" => { e with civilTime := none }
237	  | _ => e

240	  match id with
241	  | "rel.centre_distance" => { m with centreDistance := none }
242	  | "rel.surface_gap" => { m with surfaceGap := none }
243	  | "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane" => { m with aAheadOfB := none }
244	  | "rel.longitudinal_overlap" => { m with longitudinalOverlap := none }
245	  | "rel.oncoming" => { m with oncoming := none }
246	  | "rel.same_direction" => { m with sameDirection := none }
247	  | "rel.bearing" => { m with bearing := none }
248	  | "rel.contact" => { m with contact := none }
249	  | "rel.visible" => { m with visible := none }
250	  | _ => m

252	/-- Blank one atom in a scene. The computed relations are blanked through the kinematics they
253	    would be computed from only when the source lacks those too; a measured value is dropped. -/
254	def scene (id : String) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
255	  match id with
256	  | "ru.subject" => { s with subject := none }
257	  | "rel.occupies" => { s with occupancyObserved := [], occupies := [] }
258	  | "kin.time" => s
259	  | _ =>
260	    { s with users := s.users.map (user id)
261	             structures := s.structures.filterMap (structure' id)
262	             devices := s.devices.filterMap (device id)
263	             env := env id s.env
264	             relations := s.relations.map (relation id) }
265	
266	/-- Blank one atom on every road user but the subject, and in every measured relation not taken
267	    from the subject: what a source that instruments the subject's vehicle alone can say. -/
268	def sceneExceptSubject (id : String) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
269	  { s with users := s.users.map fun u => if s.subject == some u.track then u else user id u
270	           relations := s.relations.map fun m => if s.subject == some m.a then m else relation id m }
271	end Mask
272	
273	/-- The scene as the source would have produced it: every absent atom blanked, every subject-only
274	    atom blanked on everyone but the subject. -/
275	def mask (m : Manifest) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
276	  let s := m.absentIds.foldl (fun acc id => Mask.scene id acc) s
277	  m.subjectIds.foldl (fun acc id => Mask.sceneExceptSubject id acc) s
278	def maskTrace (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := τ.map (mask m)
279	
280	end TrafficSpec

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
  What a specification is: binders with class formulas, an applicability and an obligation, and
  the declarations a reviewer needs (parameters, assumptions, declared intentions,
  operationalizations, residues, narrowings, the rules it composes, the surrogate flag).

  A residue is a span of the text the rule does not capture at all; the plan declares it and the
  rule repeats it verbatim. A narrowing is a reading the coder chose on a span the plan does
  carry, stated here so the review judges the rule as it is: the span it names and why. The
  coder may add narrowings and never residues.

  Applicability and obligation are two formulas because a rule whose situation never arises is
  not compliant, it is not engaged: `notApplicable` is a verdict of its own, the witness check can
  demand a scenario for it, and a monitor reads the applicability as the trigger and the
  obligation as what to verify once triggered.

  A surrogate rule (the whole duty is an operationalized standard) is monitored like any other,
  but its verdicts are evidence about the standard, never the law's own verdict; the flag is what
  the monitor and the export propagate so the two are never summed.

  This file holds the declarations only and imports no evaluator: a rule file that imports it
  can state a rule but cannot read a scene, evaluate a formula or build evidence. Evaluation and
  the static check are in RuleEval.lean, which nothing under Rules/ may import.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Formula
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- A binder: a variable and the class formula (over `ru_*` atoms and class-level derived
    concepts) a track must satisfy to be bound to it. The subject comes first. -/
structure Binder where
  name : String
  cls : Formula
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A reading chosen on a span the record carries, declared where it is made: the span (a
    segmentation id for a rule, a run of the contract's words for a concept) and what the formulas
    state more narrowly than the words. `kind` is `reading` where the words leave the choice open,
    `observable_reading` where a word with no observable counterpart is read through the conduct
    or the feature it refers to, `no_atom` or `no_operator` where the vocabulary or the language
    cannot state the words — a declaration the gate returns for a gap, never a reading the rule
    stands on. -/
structure Narrowing where
  span : String
  why : String
  kind : String := "reading"
  deriving Repr, Inhabited, DecidableEq

structure Rule where
  id : String                                   -- the node id, derived from the law id
  laws : List String                            -- the corpus ids this rule formalizes
  binders : List Binder
  applicability : Formula
  obligation : Formula
  assumptions : List AsmId := []
  intentions : List IntId := []                 -- the declared intentions its formulas read
  operationalizations : List Operationalization := []
  residues : List String := []                  -- what the text says and the rule does not capture
  narrowings : List Narrowing := []             -- readings the coder chose on carried spans
  surrogate : Bool := false
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

inductive Verdict
  | violated
  | compliant
  | notApplicable
  | unknown (why : List UnknownReason)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

namespace Verdict
def tag : Verdict → String
  | .violated => "violated"
  | .compliant => "compliant"
  | .notApplicable => "not_applicable"
  | .unknown _ => "unknown"
def reasons : Verdict → List UnknownReason
  | .unknown w => w
  | _ => []
instance : ToString Verdict := ⟨tag⟩
end Verdict

/-- Kleene combination of the two formulas: not engaged ↦ notApplicable, engaged and the
    obligation decided ↦ compliant/violated, anything undecided ↦ unknown with its reasons. -/
def verdictAt (app obl : R) : Verdict :=
  match app.v with
  | .f => .notApplicable
  | .u => .unknown app.why
  | .t =>
    match obl.v with
    | .t => .compliant
    | .f => .violated
    | .u => .unknown obl.why

theorem verdictAt_notApplicable (app obl : R) (h : app.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .notApplicable := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [h]
theorem verdictAt_violated (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .violated := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]
theorem verdictAt_compliant (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .t) : verdictAt app obl = .compliant := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]

namespace Rule
/-- The formulas a rule consists of, class formulas first. -/
def formulas (r : Rule) : List Formula := r.binders.map (·.cls) ++ [r.applicability, r.obligation]
/-- Atom, primitive and concept names the rule reads. -/
def atoms (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.atoms).eraseDups
/-- Reading parameters the rule names. -/
def params (r : Rule) : List ParamName := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.params).eraseDups
/-- Rules the rule composes. -/
def composes (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.composed).eraseDups
/-- Assumptions the formulas read. -/
def usedAssumptions (r : Rule) : List AsmId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.assumptions).eraseDups
/-- Declared intentions the formulas read. -/
def usedIntentions (r : Rule) : List IntId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.intentions).eraseDups
def binderNames (r : Rule) : List String := r.binders.map (·.name)
def subject (r : Rule) : Option String := r.binders.head?.map (·.name)

/-- The rule and, transitively, the rules it composes (each once). -/
def closure (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List Rule :=
  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (todo : List Rule) : List Rule :=
    match fuel, todo with
    | 0, _ | _, [] => []
    | fuel + 1, x :: rest =>
      let next := x.composes.filterMap fun id =>
        if seen.contains id then none else rules.find? (·.id == id)
      x :: go fuel (seen ++ next.map (·.id)) (rest ++ next)
  go (rules.length + 1) [r.id] [r]

/-- Whether the rule reads a declared intention, in its own formulas or through a rule it
    composes at any depth. -/
def readsIntention (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  (closure rules r).any fun x => !x.usedIntentions.isEmpty
end Rule

end TrafficSpec

/-
  Witnesses for NRS_484B_127_3.

  The carriageway is the same in every scene: a highway region (10) between y = -1 m and
  y = 8.2 m, carrying two eastbound lanes, lane 11 (y 0 … 3.6 m, the right-hand lane) and lane 12
  (y 3.6 … 7.2 m); both run from x = -300 m to x = 400 m. Every file runs eastbound in lane 11 at
  y = 1.8 m, the subject (track 1) in the middle of it, and the bodies are placed by their centres
  so that the space between the nearest points of two consecutive bodies is the figure each
  narrative names: a car is 4.4 m long (half-extents 2.2 / 0.9 / 0.75 m), so a centre spacing of
  10.4 m is a 6 m space, 18.4 m a 14 m space, 29.4 m a 25 m space, 34.4 m a 30 m space and 44.4 m
  a 40 m space. Each scene declares asm.outside_business_district (false in `branch_4` only).

  Every figure here is the witness's own and appears nowhere in the rule. The reading this run
  evaluates against sets the standstill tolerance at 0.1 m/s, the file's minimum at 3 members and
  its reach at 50 m, the design vehicle at 6 m and the entry headway at 1.5 s, so the space a
  moving file owes is 6 m + 2 × 1.5 s × its speed: 66 m at 20 m/s, 30 m at 8 m/s, 21 m at 5 m/s
  and 9 m at 1 m/s. The geometry below breaks or keeps that bound by a clear margin.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_127_3
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_127_3

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n
def mps (n : Int) : Q := Units.metresPerSecond n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: v ↦ 1

/-- Half-extents: length, width, height. -/
def carExtent : Q × Q × Q := (cm 220, cm 90, cm 75)
def bikeExtent : Q × Q × Q := (cm 90, cm 30, cm 60)
/-- A 24 m combination and a 12 m bus: the entering bodies whose own length is read. -/
def truckExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 12, cm 130, m 2)
def busExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 6, cm 130, cm 160)

def highway : Structure := Build.rect 10 .highway (m (-300)) (m (-1)) (m 400) (cm 820)
def laneRight : Structure :=
  Build.lane 11 [(m (-300), m 0), (m 400, m 0), (m 400, cm 360), (m (-300), cm 360)]
    Build.east (some 12) none (some 2) (some 2)
def laneLeft : Structure :=
  Build.lane 12 [(m (-300), cm 360), (m 400, cm 360), (m 400, cm 720), (m (-300), cm 720)]
    Build.east none (some 11) (some 1) (some 2)
def carriageway : List Structure := [highway, laneRight, laneLeft]

def outsideBusinessDistrict : AsmId × Bool := ("asm.outside_business_district", true)
def insideBusinessDistrict : AsmId × Bool := ("asm.outside_business_district", false)

/-- A body in the right-hand lane, eastbound, its centre at `xCm` centimetres. -/
def inRightLane (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (xCm : Int) (speed : Q)
    (half : Q × Q × Q := carExtent) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track classes (cm xCm, cm 180) Build.east speed half

/-- A body in the left-hand lane, eastbound, its centre at `xCm` centimetres. -/
def inLeftLane (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (xCm : Int) (speed : Q)
    (half : Q × Q × Q := carExtent) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track classes (cm xCm, cm 540) Build.east speed half

/-- Five bodies one behind another in the right-hand lane at `spacing` centimetres centre to
    centre, the subject (track 1) in the middle: tracks 2 and 3 ahead of it, 4 and 5 behind. -/
def fiveInFile (classes : List RoadUserClass) (spacing : Int) (speed : Q)
    (half : Q × Q × Q := carExtent) : List RoadUser :=
  [ inRightLane 1 classes 0 speed half
  , inRightLane 2 classes spacing speed half
  , inRightLane 3 classes (2 * spacing) speed half
  , inRightLane 4 classes (-spacing) speed half
  , inRightLane 5 classes (-2 * spacing) speed half ]

/-- Three bodies one behind another, the subject in the middle. -/
def threeInFile (classes : List RoadUserClass) (spacing : Int) (speed : Q) : List RoadUser :=
  [ inRightLane 1 classes 0 speed
  , inRightLane 2 classes spacing speed
  , inRightLane 3 classes (-spacing) speed ]

/-- `forbid` (violated): Five cars of a motorcade run in file in the same lane of a two-lane highway outside a business district, declared as such by the map, at 20 m/s with longitudinal gaps of about 6 m between consecutive bodies. The space holds no entering vehicle's length plus a clear headway at that speed. -/
def forbidTrace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun _k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1)
      (fiveInFile [.motorVehicle] 1040 (mps 20))
      carriageway
      []
      (assumptions := [outsideBusinessDistrict])

/-- `permit` (compliant): five cars of the motorcade on the same highway, each holding about 40 m
    of space to its neighbours at 8 m/s: every space exceeds the 30 m an entering vehicle's length
    plus the clearance headway fore and aft comes to at that speed, by a clear 10 m. (A file at
    20 m/s cannot comply and remain a file: 66 m of space is beyond the 50 m reach within which
    this reading counts a road user as travelling in the subject's file, so the compliant scene is
    built at the lower speed.) -/
def permitTrace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun _k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1)
      (fiveInFile [.motorVehicle] 4440 (mps 8))
      carriageway
      []
      (assumptions := [outsideBusinessDistrict])

/-- `idle` (not_applicable): A pedal cycle propelled by human power, which the motor-vehicle definition leaves out, rides in close file with four others on the same highway. No motor vehicle is bound and the rule does not engage. -/
def idleTrace : Trace :=
  Build.trace 3 0 (Units.seconds 1) fun _k t =>
    Build.scene t (some 1)
      (fiveInFile [.bicycle] 280 (mps 5) bikeExtent)
      carriageway
      []
      (assumptions := [outsideBusinessDistrict])

/-- The `forbid` bodies as a source that measures the spaces between bodies but reports no
    extents would give them: the gap is a supplied measurement, and nothing in the scene lets it
    be computed from the bodies, so the manifest's mask on rel.surface_gap takes it away. -/
def blindUsers : List RoadUser :=
  (fiveInFile [.motorVehicle] 1040 (mps 20)).map fun u =>
    Build.withKin u fun k => { k with extent := none }

def supplied (a b : TrackId) (longitudinal : Q) : MeasuredRelation :=
  Build.relation a b fun r => { r with surfaceGap := some (longitudinal, Q.zero) }

  The carriageway is the same in every scene: a highway region (10) between y = -1 m and
  y = 8.2 m, carrying two eastbound lanes, lane 11 (y 0 … 3.6 m, the right-hand lane) and lane 12
  (y 3.6 … 7.2 m); both run from x = -300 m to x = 400 m. Every file runs eastbound in lane 11 at
  y = 1.8 m, the subject (track 1) in the middle of it, and the bodies are placed by their centres
  so that the space between the nearest points of two consecutive bodies is the figure each
  narrative names: a car is 4.4 m long (half-extents 2.2 / 0.9 / 0.75 m), so a centre spacing of
  10.4 m is a 6 m space, 18.4 m a 14 m space, 29.4 m a 25 m space, 34.4 m a 30 m space and 44.4 m
  a 40 m space. Each scene declares asm.outside_business_district (false in `branch_4` only).

  evaluates against sets the standstill tolerance at 0.1 m/s, the file's minimum at 3 members and
  its reach at 50 m, the design vehicle at 6 m and the entry headway at 1.5 s, so the space a
  moving file owes is 6 m + 2 × 1.5 s × its speed: 66 m at 20 m/s, 30 m at 8 m/s, 21 m at 5 m/s
  and 9 m at 1 m/s. The geometry below breaks or keeps that bound by a clear margin.

import TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B.NRS_484B_127_3
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpecWitness.NRS_484B_127_3

open TrafficSpec

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n
def cm (n : Int) : Q := Units.centimetres n
def mps (n : Int) : Q := Units.metresPerSecond n

-- Binders ↦ tracks: v ↦ 1

/-- Half-extents: length, width, height. -/
def carExtent : Q × Q × Q := (cm 220, cm 90, cm 75)
def bikeExtent : Q × Q × Q := (cm 90, cm 30, cm 60)
/-- A 24 m combination and a 12 m bus: the entering bodies whose own length is read. -/
def truckExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 12, cm 130, m 2)
def busExtent : Q × Q × Q := (m 6, cm 130, cm 160)

def highway : Structure := Build.rect 10 .highway (m (-300)) (m (-1)) (m 400) (cm 820)
def laneRight : Structure :=
  Build.lane 11 [(m (-300), m 0), (m 400, m 0), (m 400, cm 360), (m (-300), cm 360)]
    Build.east (some 12) none (some 2) (some 2)
def laneLeft : Structure :=
  Build.lane 12 [(m (-300), cm 360), (m 400, cm 360), (m 400, cm 720), (m (-300), cm 720)]
    Build.east none (some 11) (some 1) (some 2)
def carriageway : List Structure := [highway, laneRight, laneLeft]

def outsideBusinessDistrict : AsmId × Bool := ("asm.outside_business_district", true)
def insideBusinessDistrict : AsmId × Bool := ("asm.outside_business_district", false)

/-- A body in the right-hand lane, eastbound, its centre at `xCm` centimetres. -/
def inRightLane (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (xCm : Int) (speed : Q)
    (half : Q × Q × Q := carExtent) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track classes (cm xCm, cm 180) Build.east speed half

/-- A body in the left-hand lane, eastbound, its centre at `xCm` centimetres. -/
def inLeftLane (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (xCm : Int) (speed : Q)
    (half : Q × Q × Q := carExtent) : RoadUser :=
  Build.user track classes (cm xCm, cm 540) Build.east speed half

/-- Five bodies one behind another in the right-hand lane at `spacing` centimetres centre to
    centre, the subject (track 1) in the middle: tracks 2 and 3 ahead of it, 4 and 5 behind. -/
def fiveInFile (classes : List RoadUserClass) (spacing : Int) (speed : Q)
    (half : Q × Q × Q := carExtent) : List RoadUser :=
  [ inRightLane 1 classes 0 speed half
  , inRightLane 2 classes spacing speed half
  , inRightLane 3 classes (2 * spacing) speed half
  , inRightLane 4 classes (-spacing) speed half
  , inRightLane 5 classes (-2 * spacing) speed half ]

The space holds no entering vehicle's length plus a clear headway at that speed. -/

      []

# NRS_484B_127_3 — coding session result

**Final verdict: `OK`** (9 witnesses, 9 names, composes nothing, 2 narrowings declared by the coder).

## Gate runs (3 of 6 used)

| # | verdict | what changed after it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `UNUSED_CLAIM` (all nine claimed names) | the baseline skeleton, run before writing anything. Wrote the whole rule (binder class, applicability, obligation, two narrowings) and all nine witnesses. |
| 2 | `WITNESS_FAIL` — `blind`: "its trace is not one the adapter can produce: track N is in occupancy_observed but lacks a position, a non-zero heading or an extent, so its footprint is undefined" | rebuilt the `blind` scene only (see below). Nothing else was touched: the rule, the other eight witnesses, the build, the static check, the claims, the parameters and the adequacy rule had all already passed at this run. |
| 3 | `OK` | — |

### How `blind` had to be built

`Mask.relation` drops only a **supplied** `surfaceGap`; `rel_surface_gap` then falls back to the
footprints, so masking `rel.surface_gap` cannot remove a gap a scene's bodies let Core compute. A
scene whose bodies have no extents, however, is not admitted while its tracks are in
`occupancy_observed`. The witness therefore reads as a source that instruments the subject's own
vehicle and sees only the places and headings of the others: the subject has its extent and its
occupancy observed (so `rel.occupies` and the highway condition stay decided), the other four
bodies have position, heading and speed but no extent, occupancy is declared for the subject
alone, and the spaces between the bodies and which body is ahead of which are **supplied**
measurements — neither of which Core can compute in that scene, so supplying them is permitted.
Masking `rel.surface_gap` then takes the spaces away and the duty is unknown for that atom and no
other.

## Choices the node left open, and what I chose

Both are declared as `narrowings` on the rule (`kind := "reading"`) and explained in the rule's
header.

1. **s5 — "each such vehicle or combination of vehicles".** Written as every member of the
   subject's file that lies ahead of or behind it in the same lane (`rel_ahead_behind_in_lane` in
   either order, since the atom means "a is ahead of b") and within the file's reach of it (the
   space between the bodies at most `p.caravan_max_member_gap`, the reach the file concept uses).
   The record's narrowing says "immediately ahead of and behind"; the language has no operator for
   "immediately", and the space to a member further along a file is always larger than the space to
   the nearest one, so the bound on every in-reach member states the same duty and never a weaker
   one. A formula that excluded the further members (a nested "no member between them") would be a
   sub-formula no witness can move, which is why it is not written.
2. **s6 — "any other vehicle or combination of vehicles" whose length is read.** Every road user of
   the scene that is neither the subject nor a member of the subject's file; where several are
   present, the space must hold each of them, which is exactly the greater length the
   operationalization's convention names (its "max", written as a conjunction so that a scene with
   no such road user stays decided instead of going unknown on an empty aggregate).
3. **The factor of two** in `p.entry_vehicle_length + 2 × p.entry_clearance_headway_time × speed` is
   written as the headway term twice, fore and aft, because no figure of the rule file's own — not
   even a factor — may enter a formula. Noted in the header, not as a narrowing: it is syntax, not
   a reading.

Everything else follows the record: the binder's class is `ru_aggregate` with the aggregate id; the
applicability is `not standstill ∧ (∃ highway the subject occupies) ∧ vehicle_file ∧
asm.outside_business_district`; the obligation is the gap bound of s6 over those members; s4 is
carried as the record's residue and nothing reads it.

## Two places where the plan's witness declarations do not fit the plan's own reading

Neither blocked the gate — both were resolved inside the geometry, which is the witness's own — but
the plan agent should see them.

1. **`permit` cannot be the narrative's scene.** The narrative asks for the five cars "at the same
   speed" (20 m/s) with "about 70 m" of space. Under this reading's values a moving file at 20 m/s
   owes `6 + 2 × 1.5 × 20 = 66 m`, which is beyond `p.caravan_max_member_gap = 50 m`, the reach
   within which `drv.interaction.vehicle_file` counts a road user as travelling in the subject's
   file. At 20 m/s compliance and membership of the file are mutually exclusive: every compliant
   file is not a file. The `permit` witness is therefore built at 8 m/s with 40 m of space (bound
   30 m, kept by a clear 10 m); the rule file's header and the witness's doc comment say so. The
   substantive point for the plan: with these values the duty is satisfiable only below about
   14.7 m/s, so either the reach or the gap-acceptance convention is mis-scaled for highway speeds.
2. **`branch_2` expects `compliant` for a narrative that is `not_applicable`.** A halted file is
   below the standstill tolerance, so by the record's own applicability ("is moving") the rule does
   not engage and that instant's verdict is `notApplicable`, not `compliant`. The planned verdict is
   kept as the declaration requires, and the trace is a queue rolling to a halt: at the first
   instant the file is still being driven (1 m/s, 14 m of space, bound 9 m — compliant), at the two
   later instants it stands still 6 m apart and the rule does not reach it. The episode is
   `compliant` because one instant is compliant and none is violated, and the scene still shows what
   the narrative is about. If the plan meant a purely halted scene, its expected verdict should be
   `not_applicable`.

## One claim that can never decide anything

`s5` claims `ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles`, and the obligation writes it
as the second limb of the member's class disjunction, as the record maps it. In this run's reading
that aggregate has **no included classes** (every vehicle class is `unresolved`), so the atom is
never true: for a motor vehicle it is `unknown` and the disjunction is decided by the first limb,
and for anything else it is `unknown` or false. It can only ever turn a decided-false member class
into `unknown`; no witness can be decided by it. The atom is written, not deleted, as instructed.
For the plan agent: either the reading must classify some class as included under
`DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles` (a towed combination is one road user drawn by another,
which the ontology represents as `ru.trailer_or_combination`), or the claim on s5 adds nothing and
the span should rest on the motor-vehicle aggregate alone.

## Witnesses

| name | verdict | what it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `forbid` | violated | five cars, 20 m/s, 6 m of space; bound 66 m |
| `permit` | compliant | five cars, 8 m/s, 40 m of space; bound 30 m |
| `idle` | not applicable | five pedal cycles: the binder's class is decided false |
| `blind` | unknown | the forbid file with `rel.surface_gap` masked (see above) |
| `branch_1` | not applicable | one car alone: the file's minimum member count is not reached |
| `branch_2` | compliant | the file rolls to a halt: the standstill limb of s1 |
| `branch_3` | violated | a 24 m combination abreast in the left lane: `kin.extent` of a body that is no member of the file decides the bound (30 m of space, 39 m owed) |
| `branch_4` | not applicable | the forbid file inside a business district: `asm.outside_business_district` declared false |
| `branch_5` | violated | a 12 m bus 60 m ahead in the same lane, beyond the file's reach: the reach that separates a member of the file from a road user that could enter the space decides the verdict (25 m of space, 27 m owed) |

`branch_3`, `branch_4` and `branch_5` are this session's, added so that the read length of an
entering body, the business-district condition and the file's reach each move a decided witness.

## Why I finished

The gate returned `OK` on the third of six runs: the two files build, the static check and the
claim, parameter, anchoring and adequacy checks pass, and all nine witnesses reach their declared
verdicts. Three runs of budget are left and unspent, with nothing left to fix: the two items above
are the plan's to decide, not defects of the formulas, and the session's own choices are on the
rule's record as narrowings.
